title: Storefront microfrontends — full-stack feature slice
stack: Nx 24 · React 19 + rsbuild Module Federation · Tailwind v4 + shadcn · NestJS 11 microservices over TCP · NestJS gateway · Vitest + Jest · Claude Sonnet 5.5 headless in Docker
about: One storefront feature is a full-stack slice: a provider microfrontend, a NestJS TCP microservice, a shared contract library, gateway routes and tests on both sides. Three slices (catalog, cart, orders) were built first by headless agents and fixed until they ran end to end. A Project Builder `feature` schematic was then extracted from them. Three new features (reviews, wishlist, promotions) ran 3 times per arm, one fresh container per run: without-schematics gets a description of the slice, the reference features and the Nx generators; with-schematics gets the same text plus the schematic. The first schematic was measured, lost on review, was fixed, and arm B was rerun.
proves: Whether a schematic extracted from working, reviewed code makes the same agent cheaper or faster at equal quality, when the alternative is an agent that can read and copy the existing features. Decision rule, fixed before the runs: median tokens or wall time at least 30% lower, with no more structural deviations and no more review rounds.

experiments.title: Feature schematic v1 against copying a sibling
experiments.hypothesis: A schematic extracted from three reviewed features cuts median tokens or wall time by at least 30%, with no more structural deviations and no more review rounds than an agent that copies an existing feature.
experiments.variable: The with-schematics arm's context adds the feature schematic (info, execute, npm install, then only the domain). Schematic v1.
constants: Same base commit and task prompts (reviews, wishlist, promotions)
One fresh container per run, claude -p --bare
experiments.interpretation: Arm B needed 4 review rounds against 1. Five of its nine blocking findings came from the schematic itself: placeholder README rows, a JSON file rewritten with JSON.stringify, an unformatted shell entry.

experiments.title: Feature schematic v2 against copying a sibling
experiments.hypothesis: A schematic extracted from three reviewed features cuts median tokens or wall time by at least 30%, with no more structural deviations and no more review rounds than an agent that copies an existing feature.
experiments.variable: The with-schematics arm's context adds the feature schematic (info, execute, npm install, then only the domain). Schematic v2, with v1's defects fixed; arm A was not rerun.
constants: Same base commit and task prompts (reviews, wishlist, promotions)
One fresh container per run, claude -p --bare
experiments.interpretation: Both arms needed 1 review round. Arm A copied an existing feature in all nine runs, so the schematic's measured edge is cost, time and turns; four arm A runs also broke npm ci, partly because only arm B's context says to run npm install.

experiments.title: Feature schematic v2 on SDK 0.10 and Opus 5.5
experiments.hypothesis: On @pbuilder/sdk 0.10.0 and Opus 5.5, the feature schematic still cuts median tokens or wall time by at least 30% against an agent that copies an existing feature, at no worse quality gates.
experiments.variable: The with-schematics arm's context adds the feature schematic (info, execute, npm install, then only the domain). Schematic v2 on @pbuilder/sdk 0.10.0 and builder CLI 0.9.11.
constants: Same base commit and task prompts (reviews, wishlist, promotions)
One fresh container per run, claude -p --bare
Both arms rerun in the same window; no blind review this time
